<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 8 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Integrals</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">8.3</span> The Metric Volume Form</h1></header>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>Everything above holds for any volume form. On an oriented metric manifold <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}^\uparrow, g)\)</span>, the metric singles out one, the <strong>metric volume form</strong> <span class="math inline">\(\Omega^g\)</span>,  whose components in every chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X}) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)</span> are  <span class="math display" id="eq_metric_volume_form">\begin{equation}
            \big( \Omega^g_\mathscr{X} \big)_{i_1 \dots i_d} \coloneqq \sqrt{ \big| \det g_\mathscr{X} \big| } \; \varepsilon_{i_1 \dots i_d},
            \qquad
            \det g_\mathscr{X} \coloneqq \det \big( (g_\mathscr{X})_{ij} \big) \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U}), \tag{8.5}
        \end{equation}</span>  i.e. whose scalar density is  <span class="math inline">\(\omega^g_\mathscr{X} = \sqrt{|\det g_\mathscr{X}|}\)</span>,  smooth and positive since <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> is non-degenerate.  On <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}\)</span>,  with <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X}), (\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y}) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)</span>,  these components transform as those of a <span class="math inline">\((0,d)\)</span>-tensor  field<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-9" id="fnref-9" aria-label="Footnote 9">9</a></sup>:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \big( \Omega^g_\mathscr{Y} \big)_{j_1 \dots j_d}&amp; \coloneqq
            \sqrt{\big| \det g_\mathscr{Y} \big|} \; \varepsilon_{j_1 \dots j_d}
            \, \overset{\text{Ch.~7}}{=} \,
            \sqrt{\Big| \det \Big( \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)^{i}_{k} \, \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)^{j}_{l} \, (g_\mathscr{X})_{ij} \Big) \Big|} \; \varepsilon_{j_1 \dots j_d}
            \xlongrightarrow[\text{transpose: same } \det]{\det \text{ multiplicative}} ... \\
            ... =
            &amp;\sqrt{\det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)^2} \, \sqrt{\big| \det g_\mathscr{X} \big|} \; \varepsilon_{j_1 \dots j_d}
            =
            \operatorname{sgn}\big( \det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big) \big) \, \sqrt{\big| \det g_\mathscr{X} \big|} \; \det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big) \; \varepsilon_{j_1 \dots j_d}
            \xlongrightarrow{\text{(c)}} ... \\
            ... =
            &amp;\underbrace{\operatorname{sgn}\big( \det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big) \big)}_{= \, +1 \text{ in } \mathcal{A}^\uparrow} \;
            \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)^{i_1}_{j_1} \cdots \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)^{i_d}_{j_d} \,
            \underbrace{\sqrt{\big| \det g_\mathscr{X} \big|} \; \varepsilon_{i_1 \dots i_d}}_{( \Omega^g_\mathscr{X} )_{i_1 \dots i_d}}
            =
            \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)^{i_1}_{j_1} \cdots \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)^{i_d}_{j_d} \, \big( \Omega^g_\mathscr{X} \big)_{i_1 \dots i_d} .
        \end{align*}</span>  The chart-wise definitions thus agree on overlaps and define a single <span class="math inline">\((0,d)\)</span>-tensor field <span class="math inline">\(\Omega^g\)</span>, totally antisymmetric, as <span class="math inline">\(\varepsilon\)</span> is, and nowhere vanishing: a volume form. Without the orientation, the two definitions would differ by a sign wherever <span class="math inline">\(\det \big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big) &lt; 0\)</span>. If the chart-induced basis at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> is orthonormal in the sense of Sylvester’s law of inertia, <span class="math inline">\(g_{ij}(p) = 0\)</span> for <span class="math inline">\(i \neq j\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(g_{ii}(p) \in \{+1, -1\}\)</span> (Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Metric">7</a>), then <span class="math inline">\(\omega^g_\mathscr{X}(p) = 1\)</span>: <span class="math inline">\(\Omega^g\)</span> assigns unit volume to the parallelepiped spanned by an orthonormal basis.</p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p>With <span class="math inline">\(\omega^g_\mathscr{X} = \sqrt{|\det g_\mathscr{X}|}\)</span>, the integrals (<a class="dg-xref" href="integration-manifolds.html#eq_integral_chart" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_integral_chart">8.3</a>) and (<a class="dg-xref" href="integration-manifolds.html#eq_integral_manifold" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_integral_manifold">8.4</a>) become, writing <span class="math inline">\(\int_\mathcal{M} f \coloneqq \int_\mathcal{M} \Omega^g f\)</span>,  <span class="math display">\[
            \int_\mathcal{M} f
            = \sum_n \int_{\mathscr{X}_n(\mathcal{U}_n)} d^d\alpha \,
            \sqrt{ \big| \det g_{\mathscr{X}_n} \big| \big( \mathscr{X}_n^{-1}(\alpha) \big) } \; \big( (\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n f) \circ \mathscr{X}_n^{-1} \big)(\alpha) ,
        \]</span>  valid for any signature.</p></li>
</ul>
<div class="dg-footnotes"><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-9"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-9" aria-label="Back to the text">9</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>The determinants are those of the matrices of components: <span class="math inline">\(\det g_\mathscr{X}\)</span> is a function on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span>, not a scalar field, and picks up <span class="math inline">\(\det\big( \textrm{\runic ᛞ}_{\mathcal{U}\mathcal{V}} \big)^2\)</span> under a change of chart.</p></div></div></div>
